subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Opening and Closing Accounts
description: A micro-lesson that makes Opening and Closing Accounts usable.

hook.text: You hold onto a losing stock because selling it closes the mental account at a loss. Keeping it open preserves hope.

buildup.text: Closing a mental account at a loss triggers regret and finality. Keeping it open means the outcome is still 'pending.'

discovery.text: This is why people refuse to sell houses below purchase price, even when holding costs more than the difference.

twist.text: But closing a winning account feels great. This is why people sell winning investments too early: to feel the pleasure.

climax.text: The key insight: the mental account is not the investment. Close accounts based on future prospects, not past results.

punchline.text: Close the account. Keep the lesson.

quiz.question: Why do people avoid selling losing investments?
options: Closing the mental account at a loss triggers regret
Tax laws prevent selling at a loss

details.summary: Mental accounting involves opening and closing psychological accounts around purchases and experiences. People delay closing accounts with losses because it makes the loss feel permanent, while eagerly closing accounts with gains to lock in the positive feeling.
details.whyItMatters: This explains prepayment preferences, subscription resistance, and why people keep losing investments. The timing of when mental accounts are opened and closed determines the emotional experience of spending and investing.
takeaways: Prepaying creates a closed account that makes consumption feel free
People resist closing accounts that would confirm a loss
The pain of payment depends on temporal separation from consumption

faq.question: Why does an all-inclusive vacation feel so satisfying?
faq.answer: Prepaying closes the payment account before the trip begins. Each meal, drink, and activity during the vacation feels free because the mental account for payment is already settled. You enjoy consumption without the concurrent pain of paying.

faq.question: Why do people hold losing stocks instead of selling?
faq.answer: Selling closes the mental account and makes the loss official and permanent. While the stock is held, the account stays open and recovery remains possible. The pain of closing an account at a loss is psychologically worse than carrying an unrealized loss.
